system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    The promotional test grew paid conversions by 31% and monthly revenue by 18% in the low-touch segment, although the observation window was 12 weeks; the support model was the same throughout.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
The promotional test grew paid conversions by 31% and monthly revenue by 18% in the low-touch segment, although the observation window was 12 weeks; the support model was the same throughout.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to answer with promotional_pricing, and memory_73 looks like the strongest single result in the inherited record (+31% paid conversions, +18% monthly revenue). But that memory carries its own hedges forward: a 12-week observation window and an unchanged support model. Neither of those supports a claim about durable, qualified revenue — a 12-week window can't distinguish real expansion from pull-forward of conversions that would have happened anyway, and discount-acquired accounts in a price-sensitive segment are exactly the cohort most likely to churn or to be low-margin. Matching a competitor on price also tends to select for the least loyal accounts, which cuts against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. So I want the source record for memory_73 specifically to see retention and revenue-quality data past the window, and I am treating it as unverified rather than as a mandate until then.

The two metrics actually moving against us are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and three inherited memories point at that surface: memory_31 (signup simplification lifted SMB activation, described as durable), memory_86 (shorter onboarding improved completion and time-to-value), and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement). simplify_onboarding sits at the intersection — it directly targets the declining completion metric and is upstream of activation, so it plausibly addresses both. I prefer it to activation_messaging because messaging treats a symptom further down the funnel while completion is degrading upstream. I second-verify memory_31 because its 'durable lift' claim is the load-bearing part of my choice and it was consolidated at day 12, the oldest record here; the product and funnel may have changed enough that it no longer transfers.

Noted downstream risk on my own pick: cutting required fields at signup can improve activation while degrading lead qualification data and routing, which would quietly hurt qualified pipeline even as the headline metrics improve. memory_44 is a reminder that enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted path, so I will scope this to the self-serve/SMB flow only and leave the demo-request path untouched, and I will instrument revenue quality and 90-day retention rather than only completion and activation. Standard experiment scale with a holdout: the evidence is suggestive and directionally consistent across three memories, but none of it is confirmed post-verification, so I do not want a broad rollout, and a small guarded test would not resolve a 4-6% movement.
